'''Robert Carr Dynes''' (8 November 1942 – 30 June 2025) was a Canadian-American physicist. He served as the 18th president of the [[University of California]] from 2003 to 2007 and as the 6th chancellor of the [[University of California, San Diego]] from 1996 to 2003.

==Biography==
===Early life and education===
Dynes was born in [[Ontario]], Canada, where he earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics and physics from the [[University of Western Ontario]] in 1964. He then earned his master's (1965) and doctorate (1968) degrees in physics from [[McMaster University]].  He became a naturalized United States citizen in 1984.

===Career ===
Dynes worked at [[Bell Laboratories]] from 1964 to 1990 studying [[semiconductors]] and [[superconductors]].  He then became professor of physics at the [[University of California, San Diego]] in 1991. He became chancellor of the University of California, San Diego in 1996 and was chosen in 2003 to serve the 18th president of the University of California system.

Dynes' scientific honors included the 1990 Fritz London Memorial Prize in Low Temperature Physics and his 2001 election to the Council of the National Academy of Sciences.

Dynes was also a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (1981),<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1981&unit_id=&institution=Bell+Laboratories}} (search on year=1981 and institution=Bell Laboratories)</ref> the [[Canadian Institute for Advanced Research]], and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].  
Dynes stayed active in research and headed a modest-sized low-temperature physics laboratory at [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]].

After five tumultuous years as the president of the University of California, filled with compensation scandals, the suicide of the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]] chancellor [[Denice Denton]] and other challenges,<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20071201035114/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2007/08/14/DYNES.TMP SF Chronicle Scandal Mars UC Chief Legacy]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sanfranmag.com/story/scandal-scapegoats-and-suicide |title=San Francisco Magazine Scandals Scapegoats and Suicide |access-date=14 December 2008 |archive-date=29 March 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100329015926/http://www.sanfranmag.com/story/scandal-scapegoats-and-suicide |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://chronicle.com/news/article/2851/u-of-californias-president-robert-dynes-to-resign-after-tumultuous-5-years Five Tumultuous Years]</ref> on 13 August 2007, Dynes announced he would resign his presidency, return to his teaching position, and spend time with his new wife, Ann Parode. He resigned on 16 August 2007, and was succeeded by [[Mark Yudof]], a former chancellor of the [[University of Texas system]].

In November 2008, Dynes' close aide and his UC associate president Linda Morris Williams was<!-- If you believe that this is the wrong verb form, see Talk, under "Grammaticality", before you edit it. --> awarded a controversial payout<ref>SF Chronicle "Severance, new UC job for aide in pay scandal" https://www.sfgate.com/news/article/Severance-new-UC-job-for-aide-in-pay-scandal-3183821.php</ref><ref>California State Auditor Report 2006-103, 2 May 2006 http://www.bsa.ca.gov/reports/2006-103/employees/232.html</ref> and re-hired as an associate chancellor at the University of California, Berkeley by chancellor [[Robert Birgeneau]]. This event led president [[Mark Yudof]] to make changes to the buyout program.<ref>Sf Chronicle "UC Chief Changes Buyout Plan"[http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/object/article?f=/c/a/2008/12/03/MNH614GCU0.DTL&o=2]{{dead link|date=February 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>San Diego Reader "After the Fall" http://www.sandiegoreader.com/news/2008/dec/10/breaking-news-1/</ref>

===Personal life and death===
Dynes became a naturalized United States citizen in 1984. He married Cristel Dynes in 1968, but they divorced in January 1998. He married a physics professor, [[Frances Hellman]],<ref name="sandiegoreader.com">San Diego Reader "UCSD Big Money and Ball Club" http://www.sandiegoreader.com/news/2000/feb/24/ucsd-big-money-and-ball-club/</ref> in May 1998, but they also divorced in 2006. He married a former UCSD legal counsel and UC Associate of the President, Ann Parode Dynes,<ref>[http://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/regents/regmeet/mar07/r.pdf Appointment of Ann Parode Dynes as Associate of the President March 2007 Regent Minutes]</ref> in March 2007.<ref name="sandiegoreader.com"/>

Dynes died on 30 June 2025, at the age of 82.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-30 |title=University of California mourns the passing of former UC President Robert C. Dynes {{!}} University of California |url=https://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/press-room/university-california-mourns-passing-former-uc-president-robert-c-dynes |access-date=2025-07-01 |website=www.universityofcalifornia.edu |language=en}}</ref>
